results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of discs evolving to polar

evidence.quote: found to be 46%

findings_qualitative.value: The disc is in a polar configuration; the moderately misaligned alternative is reoriented within hundreds of years.

evidence.quote: the moderately misaligned configuration is reoriented on a timescale that is very short relative to the ten million-year old age of the system

claims.hypothesis: Is the HD 98800BaBb disc strongly misaligned and polar?
claims.experiment: Visibility modelling of ALMA data plus SPH simulations of both inclination solutions
claims.result: Inclination 26 or 154 deg; 154 deg is 4 deg from polar; the 26 deg case reorients to polar in hundreds of years
claims.finding: The disc is in a stable polar configuration

evidence.quote: We therefore conclude that the disc is in the polar configuration

claims.hypothesis: Is the disc gas-rich and planet-forming?
claims.experiment: n-body test particles plus CO and dust masses
claims.result: Particles are ejected within 1 Myr without gas; gas mass comparable to dust
claims.finding: Disc is likely gas-rich and protoplanetary, with gas more extended than dust

evidence.quote: HD 988000BaBb almost certainly harbours a long-lived gas-rich protoplanetary disc.

claims.result: About 46% of discs evolve to polar
claims.finding: Polar circumbinary planets may be common

evidence.quote: found to be 46%

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Moderately misaligned (26 deg) configuration rejected because it reorients on short timescales.

evidence.quote: the lifetime of the disc in the moderately misaligned case is very short relative to the stellar age of ten million years

limitations_admitted.value: Gas and dust mass estimates have large systematic uncertainties from optical depth, temperature and H2/CO.

evidence.quote: the empirical evidence for which dominates remains uncertain

referee_caveats_inferred: Inclination ambiguity resolved only by dynamical argument
Simple power-law ring model; optically thick emission ignored
SPH simulations exclude the outer binary and have no stated resolution tests
Population estimate assumes uniform initial orientations
